newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: World leaders descend on Bangladesh for anniversary.
newsitem.headline: World leaders descend on Bangladesh for anniversary.

text.p: The presidents of Turkey, the Palestinian Authority and South Africa arrived in Dhaka on Tuesday to attend celebrations marking Bangladesh's 26th independence anniversary.
Suleyman Demirel of Turkey was the first to arrive, followed by Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat and South Africa's Nelson Mandela. The celebrations are due to take place on Wednesday.
Artillery fired 19 shots in honour of each of the leaders as they landed at Dhaka airport to a red carpet reception.
Ceremonial motorcades took the leaders to the Dhaka Sheraton in the city centre where they are staying under tight security.
Bangladesh proclaimed independence from Pakistan on March 26, 1971, and was liberated on December 16 the same year after a nine-month war in which it was helped by India.

The leaders will fly to the independence war mausoleum at Savar, 40 km (25 miles) from Dhaka, early on Wednesday before attending a function at the historic Dhaka garden where independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman called for resistance against the Pakistani army in 1971.
Mujib, father of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and the first president of Bangladesh, was assassinated with most of his family in a military coup in August 1975.
The leaders would meet separately with Hasina on Tuesday, foreign ministry officials said. They leave on Thursday.
